# Decision Record: Benchmark task fixture copies exclude generated bytecode

Status: implemented

## Problem

Parallel benchmark scenarios import a provider from the shared task source while other scenarios copy that tree into isolated datasets. Python creates and replaces bytecode files during import. Copying a temporary bytecode entry after directory enumeration can fail before a lifecycle trial starts, even though all authored task inputs remain available.

## Decision

The test-only `benchmark/test/fixtures/task_copy.py` owns task copying for Docker lifecycle, native matrix and oracle fixtures. It excludes `__pycache__` directories and `*.pyc` files while using the ordinary strict copy operation for authored inputs. Missing task roots and disappearing real source files still fail. Dataset copies retain source and dotfile bytes; production dataset snapshots and task preparation are unchanged.

A filesystem regression removes a listed entry synchronously after enumeration. The two bytecode cases reproduce the failure without threads, sleeps or retries, while negative controls preserve failures for a missing root or disappearing provider source. Native timeout, terminal-evidence, cleanup and resume assertions retain their existing budgets and execution paths.

## Alternatives considered

**Serialize scenario workers or disable Python bytecode globally.** These choices alter unrelated execution and preparation instead of defining which files constitute task fixture inputs. Scenario isolation does not require serializing immutable authored source reads.

**Retry the entire copy or ignore every missing file.** A retry can conceal real source changes, and a broad missing-file fallback can publish an incomplete task. Only generated bytecode is excluded.

**Filter only the failing lifecycle copy.** Matrix and oracle copies read the same provider tree and remain exposed to the same import race. One small test helper keeps their input policy consistent without changing the evaluator.

## Consequences

Parallel fixture setup no longer depends on generated Python cache-file lifetimes. The test helper and its deterministic controls add a small shared test dependency. Bytecode is rebuilt as needed in each disposable environment. Passing copy controls do not establish native lifecycle correctness or infrastructure readiness; Docker preparation failures and unexecuted lifecycle controls remain separate verification limits.
